text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's collective cabinet protests to the international community's High Representative in Bosnia, Carl Bildt, for not being officially invited to the upcoming Viena conference on implementation of arbitration over the disputed town of Brcko.
- Moslem-Croat federation makes more progress in establishing trade unions than the Serb Republic, the Public Service International (PSI) told a press conference in Sarajevo on Wednesday.
- The trial of four Bosnian army soldiers will begin on March 10 at the International Criminal Tribunal for Former Yugoslavia in the Hague, newspaper says.
- Sarajevo will host a symposium on civil engineering achievements organised by Germany from March 12 to 14.

- Newspaper sources close to the International Criminal Tribunal for Former Yugoslavia in the Hague say that the tribunal demands from Croatia to extradite Bosnian Croat warlord Mladen Naletilic-Tuta to the tribunal.
- Bosnia's health workers go on general strike on Thursday throughout Bosnia after federal government failed to meet their demands, health workers' union says.
